  "insights": [
   "Specialist sales desk (not Research) says global markets are trading risk off as oil volatility rises and early mega-cap earnings disappoint. It argues commodity conditions have deteriorated meaningfully in recent sessions.",
   "Efforts to ease bottlenecks in freight and diesel have done little to stop price increases. Gulf attacks have grown in frequency and scope, and US and Israeli escalation increasingly looks like the base case.",
   "Iran reports seven oil tankers caught fire or were damaged in the Strait overnight (unconfirmed). The market is already short freight, so tanker damage tightens it further.",
   "Yesterday's attack on Shaybah (1mbd) is the latest sign that Saudi energy infrastructure is now in scope as it had not been earlier in the conflict. Operations were reportedly unaffected. The Houthi/Saudi conflict is splintering.",
   "Embassy evacuations and Israeli fighter jet trials aimed at provoking Iran add to the case for abandoning de-escalation hopes. The 2027 WTI strip is pushing $88, a wartime high.",
   "Counterweight: a WSJ article says Iranian oil on water has fallen from about 90mb to under 1 million since the US reimposed its blockade. Centcom says the blockade has denied Tehran about $25bn of oil revenue.",
   "Vortexa estimates about 6 million barrels of Iranian oil sat off Singapore as of Oct. 9. Chinese refiners are turning to Brazil and West Africa, which the author sees as a structural threat to Iranian revenue even if the blockade is lifted. Oil is 30-40% of Iranian government revenue.",
   "Russian crude processing rose to just over 3.7m b/d on Oct. 8-14, up about 50kbd from the first week of the month, as repaired plants offset lower runs at Omsk. Investors are skeptical about a ramp into year-end. Russia has said it could reach 3-3.5 metric tons of exports a month by year-end.",
   "The API estimates global refineries are processing about 3.3mbd less than last year even after US and rest-of-world run increases, so the market needs the Russian runs.",
   "EU gas: NWE+UK demand averaged 454 Mcm/day for Oct 12-18, up 13% WoW on colder weather, mostly in Germany. Month-to-date demand is 406 Mcm/day, about 20% lower YoY and 60 Mcm/day below JPM forecasts, driven by residential demand. October weather is about 0.2 stdev warmer than normal and the November outlook is 1.1 stdev warmer.",
   "Asia LNG imports are on track for a three-month high in October despite spot prices at their highest in almost four years, per Kpler.",
   "KMI beat on 3Q adj. EBITDA and raised its outlook, with the project backlog rising to $14.4bn. JPM expects a positive reaction but notes that 6-8% MTD outperformance versus WMB and DTM may limit the move and that investor feedback was mixed.",
   "LBRT announced an agreement with an unnamed frontier AI lab for 1.2 GW of integrated power services. JPM expects a positive reaction, with a 500 MW ESA targeted by December 2026 and a significant capacity-fee prepayment in 4Q. Counterparty financial strength and contract length (CEO has messaged 15-year minimums) are the questions for the call.",
   "KALU missed 3Q adj. EBITDA and guided FY26 EBITDA to the lower end of its range. FY26 FCF guidance was raised. JPM rates KALU Underweight.",
   "VLO rose 2% pre-market on the 3Q print, which the desk calls slightly light. EPS beat versus Street was the smallest since 2Q24 and revenue was the first miss since 4Q23. Renewable Diesel segment was weak. Short positioning had already cleaned up into the print.",
   "PCG fell 2% in pre-market as its data center pipeline grew only modestly after last quarter's 7.6GW increase. FY guidance was reaffirmed and the desk still views PCG as a held long versus EIX.",
   "Reliance reported a strong 3Q beat and 4Q guide above Street on record shipments and pricing. JPM rates it Neutral.",
   "Fortescue is in a price deadlock with CMRG, which has barred domestic mills from taking Super Special Fines (about 43% of FY26 shipments). Inventory is building at about 5Mt a month. JPM cut FY27 NPAT 15% but kept its $22 valuation and Overweight rating.",
   "Crescent Energy (CRGY) agreed to buy DVN's Eagle Ford assets for about $3.85B, adding about 68 MBoe/d. JPM sees it lifting royalty cash flow by more than 25%.",
   "Pre-earnings views: TC Energy is expected to beat and raise with 2027 guidance and Crossroads FID in focus. AltaGas is modeled above the high end of its 2026 EBITDA guidance.",
   "Hudbay and Mitsubishi approved construction of the Copper World project in Arizona, with production starting in the back half of 2029.",
   "Headline flow: US and Israel are reportedly drafting plans for resumed strikes on Iran after the midterms. IRGC says four oil vessels hit mines near Hormuz. Middle East oil exports are back near prewar levels per FT and Bloomberg. The US is releasing Northeast heating oil reserves."

  "insights": [
   "USD 10y rates have retraced just over 30bp from their highs as cracks appear in higher-yielding credit and equities rotate heavily. The AI vs AI-at-risk basket is down on the year.",
   "AI capex has been central to the US outlook and the duration sell-off this year. The AI complex has now shown some sensitivity to higher yields, which caps sharp rate sell-offs. The left tail of a sharper AI downturn has fattened slightly.",
   "With the recent equity-rates correlation, long duration is again a hedge for a long equity portfolio. A sustained larger rate rally needs a further fall in equity indices (not just rotation) or a sharper FCI tightening, which is not the base case.",
   "A supply/demand imbalance drove US yields higher this year. Lower AI-related supply and portfolio hedging demand slightly reduce it but do not solve it. The imbalance persists unless the AI capex outlook collapses.",
   "Fed: September inflation data would on most playbooks have pushed the committee toward an October hike. The Fed instead uniformly played down October, tilted toward gradualism by credit moves and equity rotation, and gave forward guidance.",
   "GS base case is still a December Fed hike, but pricing is unlikely to return toward a full 25bp because the asymmetry favors receiving December as a hedge against further equity capitulation. The path beyond December is hard to call.",
   "GIR sees US core inflation already through its peak, with tariff effects fading through next year and the AI inflation impact peaking by year-end, only 5bp more than the current impact.",

   "Rabobank expects the FOMC to hold the target range at 3.75-4.00% at the October 27-28 meeting.",
   "Rabobank expects Hammack, Kashkari and Logan to repeat their July dissents in favor of a hike, so the hold is not unanimous.",
   "Chair Warsh is expected to keep refusing forward guidance at the press conference but to do so in a hawkish way, as at Jackson Hole. He may say underlying inflation trends have not meaningfully improved without saying a hike is coming soon.",

   "Skipping October lets the Committee see more data, and a December hike would bring the funds rate to the median participant's year-end projection. Skipping also avoids a hike less than a week before the midterm elections. President Trump has said he wants lower rates.",

  "title": "Winners And Losers If The Data-Center Buildout Is Delayed",
  "type": "sector",
  "priority": "high",
  "published": "2026-10-27",
  "insights": [
   "Compute demand is significantly greater than supply, so the speed of the data center buildout determines who benefits and who is hurt.",
   "Winners from a slower buildout are assets tied to scarce physical capacity: operating data centers, hyperscalers with power, land and chips already secured, holders of powered land and grid access, long-lead equipment makers, and power producers with on-site generation.",
   "Operating data centers can raise rents and fill every megawatt because new competitors cannot arrive quickly.",
   "Powered land with secured power, interconnection and permits is described as the scarcest input and hardest to replicate, so its value rises in a delay.",
   "Long-lead equipment suppliers (transformers, switchgear, generators, cooling) keep long backlogs and pricing power, with transformer lead times of up to 26 months.",
   "Where the grid is the bottleneck, gas turbines, fuel cells and batteries become more valuable.",
   "Hyperscaler growth and earnings lose in a delay: revenue is capped by supply rather than demand, committed capex keeps accruing while capacity sits idle, and pricing power on existing capacity only partly offsets this.",
   "AI labs, startups and enterprise buyers face rationing, higher prices and slower model training and product launches, with smaller players crowded out first.",
   "Developers and construction-stage investors see cash flows start later while interest and carrying costs continue. Leveraged or pre-lease-dependent developers face covenant and refinancing stress.",
   "Equity investors in the AI trade are exposed to earnings revisions and multiple compression, because valuations assume on-time delivery.",
   "The broader economy loses: near-term GDP growth, which leans on AI investment, is lower, AI productivity gains arrive later, and households and businesses on the same grid may see higher electricity costs.",
   "Chipmakers face a mixed outcome: chip demand stays strong, but if sites cannot energize fast enough, chip deliveries could outrun installation and delay revenue. The risk is mainly timing.",
   "Delay versus cancellation is the key distinction. A delay pushes cash flows out but the asset remains and may become more valuable. The real risk is scarcity unwinding, for example if supply catches up in a rush or demand softens, which would erode the premium on existing capacity.",
   "Hyperscaler bonds face mostly spread risk rather than default risk. The broader market is exposed through the weight of AI names in major indices and through slower growth."

  "type": "macro",

  "published": "2026-10-27",
  "insights": [
   "Excess liquidity (real money growth versus economic growth) has been falling for several months and is starting to weigh on global risk assets.",
   "Excess liquidity operates with a three-to-six month lag, so the current period is when its impact is likely to be most noticeable.",
   "The decline in excess liquidity is not driven by money growth. US M1 recently lifted the G10 median money growth. The cause is the lagged effect of a pick-up in growth and, more so, inflation.",
   "Money growth cannot be read in isolation. Part is absorbed by real economic growth and part by inflation. Only the remainder is available to support markets, and that portion is small.",
   "The framework explains why higher oil prices are ultimately negative for stocks: they raise inflation, which absorbs liquidity.",
   "Cracks are showing in the AI trade. Proximate causes include compute overcapacity concerns, and the remote cause is the squeeze on excess liquidity.",
   "The liquidity squeeze is unlikely to ease until monetary policy loosens or a new AI narrative revives animal spirits, unlocking more savings or boosting bank credit."
